text:
alex: FYI security bulletin just posted — multiple vulnerabilities affecting inference stack: vLLM, Triton kernels, FlashAttention, protobuf, sentencepiece. link: https://security.example.com/advisory/2026-rr-inference
mira: link? can someone summarize which ones are remote-exec vs local-privilege? :eyes:
devon: quick read: protobuf CVE-2026-0001 is RCE from crafted messages (affects our preproc service), vLLM CVE-2026-0002 is memory corruption on certain sequence lengths, flash kernel CVE-2026-0003 is local escalation in cuda kernel context (requires ledger access). sentencepiece CVE-2026-0004 is low-impact parser overflow.
samir: priority mapping i propose:
- CVE-2026-0001 (protobuf) -> P0 (public-facing preprocessors ingest untrusted payloads)
- CVE-2026-0002 (vLLM) -> P1 (high exploit complexity but impacts hosted API under heavy prefix)
- CVE-2026-0003 (Flash kernels) -> P1 (affects dedicated/private where kernels run, but needs local gpu access)
- CVE-2026-0004 (sentencepiece) -> P2
security-bot: Advisory ingested: CVE-2026-0001..0004. Suggested fixes: protobuf 3.21.9+, vLLM patch v0.9.5, FlashAttention hotpatch v2.1.1, sentencepiece 0.1.96.
alex: good mapping. two operational asks: 1) confirm if protobuf bump is ABI-compatible with our compiled wheels (we ship many wheels in private deploys) 2) any KMS/RBAC impact if we rotate keys during patch window?
mira: protobuf bump may require rebuild of our manylinux wheel for models preproc image. rolling hotpatch in hosted is straightforward (rebuild image -> canary -> promote) but Dedicated/private customers expect binary-level compatibility.
devon: for KMS: rotating keys while doing canary creates a window where older nodes might fail to decrypt cached KV entries. we should sequence: stop old nodes, rotate, boot new nodes with rotated keys OR support dual-key decrypt for short window. need to coordinate with platform.
samir: also audit logging change: record key-id used for each KV decrypt and record package upgrade events. make sure logs flow to S3 for 365-day retention for compliance.
oncall-sre: note: Triton + CUDA driver bump required for FlashAttention patched kernels. that adds infra risk: host driver upgrade needs reboot. timeline ~2 hrs maintenance per pool.
alex: plan proposal:
- immediate: protobuf patch in hosted preprocessors today (canary 10% -> 100%), create PR to rebuild wheels and upload to internal registry. tag as P0.
- short (48h): vLLM upgrade in staging with extended evals (long-tail seq tests) + quantized path smoke tests.
- next workday: schedule Triton/FlashAttention upgrade for dedicated pools with driver maintenance window. coordinate with customer ops and CAP.
- sentencepiece to be batched into next weekly minor release.
mira: testing checklist (I'll own):
- unit + fuzz for protobuf parser
- long-seq decode stress on vLLM (100k tokens across 10k requests)
- quantized kernels validation matrix: int8/int4/FP16
- Triton perf regression sweep (latency P50/P95) and canary traffic 5 minutes on real traffic
- KMS decrypt dual-key smoke

devon: I'll open infra tickets: rebuild-manylinux-wheel, driver-upgrade-runbook, dual-key-decrypt flag in runtime.
samir: security tasks:
- prepare CVE notices for customers (which deployments affected + mitigation steps)
- update RBAC playbook so only ops role can rotate KMS keys during maintenance
- ensure audit events: package_upgrade, key_rotate, decrypt_failure

alex: timeline: start protobuf patch now; i'll ping infra channel when canary ready. anyone seeing blockers?
mira: blocked on CI artifacts for manylinux wheels — building now, ETA ~1.5h.
oncall-sre: I'll reserve 3h maintenance window tomorrow 01:00-04:00 UTC for driver + Triton; will post to status page and DM affected PMs.
security-bot: CVE-2026-0001 fix verified in staging. awaiting canary results.
alex: perfect. devon/samir/mira — let's sync 30m after canary start. :thumbsup:
